data.title: Canada Posts Budget Deficit in September on Public-Debt Charges — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada's budget deficit in September was largely unchanged from the same year-ago month, as a solid gain in personal-tax revenue was partly offset by hefty public-debt charges.

Canada's Department of Finance said the budget deficit in September stood at 5.14 billion Canadian dollars (US$3.61 billion), a slight rise from the year-ago C$5.02 billion shortfall. After the first six months of the current fiscal year, Ottawa is running a C$10.50 billion budget deficit, narrower compared with the C$16.09 billion from the same year-ago period.

The September data arrived weeks after the Liberal government's annual budget plan, which contemplates roughly C$140 billion in spending over the next half decade to fortify an economy struggling under the weight of U.S. tariffs. That spending is being partly financed by higher crude-oil prices, as Canada is a net exporter of the commodity.

The recent budget plan anticipates annual deficits of C$50 billion to C$60 billion, or under 2% of gross domestic product, over the next half-decade. The five-year forecast assumes average annual growth of just under 2%, and crude-oil prices averaging C$74 a barrel, or about 20% below current levels.

The public-finance data, available through the department's Fiscal Monitor publication, said total tax revenue in September rose 3.4% from a year ago. A 10% gain in personal-tax receipts was offset by a decline in sales-tax receipts, which officials attributed to the timing of assessments and refunds issued in the month.

Total expenses in September rose 5.1%. That was driven by a 10.4% increase in public-debt charges, due to higher average rates on an increased stock of bonds. Yields have climbed globally, reflecting expectations of higher inflation--fueled by elevated energy prices--and worries about sovereign debt levels.

The Canadian parliament's budget watchdog said in a report this month that a planned increase in nonbudgetary transactions contemplated by Prime Minister Mark Carney means the debt will grow about three times faster than the deficit over the next five years. This might leave federal finances exposed to unexpected rises in rates, the watchdog said.

data.title: Uganda launches Africa's first trial of an mRNA Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine
data.description:
Uganda said on Friday that it had launched Africa's first clinical trial of an mRNA vaccine against the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus, which is behind the outbreak centred on Congo that is now the second-largest on record globally.

  • In a statement the state-run Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI) said it had launched the trial in collaboration with Moderna , which manufactures the vaccine

  • Moderna's vaccine will also enter trials in Congo soon, alongside another new vaccine targeting Bundibugyo developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India

  • Scientists are already testing if an existing vaccine targeting a different Ebola virus, Merck's Ervebo, can provide any cross-protection against Bundibugyo

  • The Ugandan trial is the second for the vaccine, after Moderna began its first human trial of the shots in Canada in August, targeting adults from 18 to 65 years of age

  • UVRI said the Ugandan trial will for the first time test the vaccine's safety and ability to trigger an immune response in children aged 1 year and above, and aims to enroll 224 volunteers

  • "Children are often among those hardest hit when Ebola strikes, yet they are too often the last to benefit from new vaccines," said Richard Hatchett, chief executive officer of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, which is helping fund the vaccine

data.title: Austrian court turns ex-tycoon Benko's suspended sentence into 6 months' prison
data.description:
An Austrian appeals court turned fallen property tycoon Rene Benko's suspended 15-month sentence for insolvency-related fraud into six months in prison on Friday, a court spokesperson said.

  • A lower court in Benko's home city of Innsbruck convicted him on December 10, 2025, of hiding valuables from creditors, including two luxury watches and cuff links found in a safe, his second conviction for insolvency-related fraud. His sentence also included a fine of €4,320 ($4,743)

  • Since then, he was convicted at a retrial in September of a second count in his first criminal case, increasing his sentence in that case to 30 months from an original two years, of which he has now served 22 months

  • Benko was convicted of aggravated fraud this month in a third criminal trial, and sentenced to an additional two years in prison. He is appealing that decision

  • Benko is currently under house arrest, wearing an ankle monitor, in Innsbruck

  • Friday's decision by the appeals court in Innsbruck, which effectively replaced the original suspended sentence and fine at first instance with the six-month prison sentence, took into account the increased sentence at retrial in September, a spokesperson for the court said

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: Sony Unveils Spatial Audio Microphone For Smartphones With Eclipsa Audio Certification
data.description:
Priced at Rs 17,990

The ECM-AX10 is a compact, lightweight microphone that connects directly to compatible smartphones via USB-C, offering three recording modes: Ambisonics for full spatial audio production, binaural for immersive headphone playback, and stereo for everyday videos and social media content. Paired for YouTube via the “Spatial Audio Video Tool” app, creators can record videos, review footage, make basic edits and export content with spatial audio, enabling an end-to-end spatial audio video production workflow directly on their smartphones.

The Sony ECM-AX10 helps creators capture rich, high-quality audio that can be integrated into Eclipsa Audio immersive sound productions. Combined with Eclipsa Audio's open spatial audio technology, it enables a more realistic and engaging listening experience across next generation TVs, soundbars, and digital content platforms.

Key product features:

Spatial audio for smartphone video

The ECM-AX10 is designed to make smartphone videos sound natural and true to the moment. Sony’s newly developed spherical microphone module uses four omnidirectional microphone capsules to support Ambisonics recording, helping capture sound from all around the scene. With advanced spatial audio processing, creators can bring through the atmosphere, direction and distance of a place, from street performances and festivals to sports, travel content and behind-the-scenes moments, so viewers feel closer to the action.

Three recording modes for different creator approaches

Creators can choose from three recording modes to suit their content, platform and playback needs. Ambisonics recording works with the Spatial Audio Video Tool app to support publishing in Eclipsa Audio for an immersive audio experience on YouTube. Binaural recording uses Sony’s proprietary spatial audio technology, also used for 360 Reality Audio, to create a headphone-optimised three-dimensional sound experience. Stereo recording offers a versatile format for headphones and speakers. The microphone can also be used with general recording and video apps as well as Sony’s dedicated apps.

Compact USB-C design for filming on the move

Weighing approximately 24g, the ECM-AX10 is designed to be carried anywhere and set up quickly for spontaneous filming. The direct USB-C connection helps creators capture higher-quality audio without a separate recorder or complex setup, supporting a simple smartphone-first production workflow. With the Spatial Audio Video Tool app, users can record video, review clips, make quick edits and export finished content with spatial audio entirely on their smartphone, streamlining the journey from capture to share.

Developed with sound engineers

To help ensure the ECM-AX10 delivers an authentic and immersive listening experience, Sony collaborated with its post-production subsidiary, Sony PCL, a Sony Group company with extensive expertise in planning and producing content and spatial experiences.

Pricing and Availability

The ECM-AX10 is  available on E- Commerce Portal, Selected Sony Centres and Pro Audio Stores.

data.title: Sensex Falls Nearly 1,000 Pts, Nifty Slips As IT, Financial Stocks Drag Markets Lower
data.description:
The Sensex declines 989.33 points, or 1.17 per cent, to settle at 83,339.26, while the Nifty falls 1.07 per cent, to close at 25,607

Indian equity benchmarks snapped their two-session winning streak on Friday, November 27, as rising crude oil prices, a weaker rupee and selling pressure in heavyweight stocks weighed on investor sentiment. The Nifty closed below 25,650, with losses accelerating towards the end of the session amid sustained profit booking.

The Sensex declined 989.33 points, or 1.17 per cent, to settle at 83,339.26, while the Nifty fell 277.30 points, or 1.07 per cent, to close at 25,607.20. The Nifty touched an intraday low of 25,590.45, ending the session close to that level after a volatile start and selling pressure in the final hours.

The weakness also affected weekly performance. Both the Sensex and the Nifty declined 0.7 per cent over the week, ending their four-week winning streak.

“Autos and IT were the key laggards, with IT surrendering part of its recent gains. Near-term consolidation remains likely, as Q3FY27 earnings growth is expected to moderate and uncertainty over proposed US tariffs persists. Nevertheless, strong foreign inflows and expectations of 7.7 per cent Q2FY27 GDP growth continue to support a constructive medium-term outlook,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments.

IT, Realty, Auto Stocks Lead Losses

Information technology stocks bore the brunt of the selling, with the Nifty IT index plunging nearly 2 per cent. Realty stocks also remained under pressure, with the Nifty Realty index declining 1.4 per cent. The Nifty Auto index fell 1.5 per cent, while the Nifty Private Bank index lost 1 per cent.

In contrast, defence and metal stocks provided some support. The Nifty Defence index advanced more than 3 per cent, while the Nifty Metal index gained 1.4 per cent. The Nifty Media index edged up 0.5 per cent.

Among Nifty 50 constituents, Shriram Finance, Bajaj Auto, HCL Technologies, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys were the biggest laggards. Bharat Electronics, JSW Steel, Titan, Hindalco Industries and SBI Life Insurance featured among the leading gainers.

Mid- and Small-cap Stocks Outperform

Broader markets showed greater resilience than the benchmark indices. The Nifty Midcap index edged up 0.1 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap index advanced 0.5 per cent, ending in positive territory despite the sharp decline in the Sensex and Nifty.

Among individual stocks, Supriya Lifescience rose 7 per cent after its board announced plans to consider a share buyback proposal. Zydus Lifesciences declined more than 3 per cent after receiving a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) for its saroglitazar application.

Syrma SGS and Avalon Technologies gained more than 1 per cent each after JPMorgan upgraded both stocks to 'Neutral'.

Kalyan Jewellers advanced 3 per cent after HSBC maintained its 'Buy' recommendation with a target price of Rs 830 per share. International Gemmological Institute gained 1.5 per cent, with 67.16 lakh shares changing hands during the session.

data.title: JW Marriott Pune hosts Malaysian chef Johnson Wong for culinary collaboration
data.description:
JW Marriott Pune will host Malaysian chef Johnson Wong, founder of gēn, Malaysia, for a two-day culinary collaboration at its Chinese restaurant Tao-Fu on November 27 and 28, 2026. The experience, titled ‘The Search for Home: Anchoring Heritage in Modern Craft’, is presented in association with Gormei.

Wong has worked across France, Denmark, Macau and Singapore before returning to Malaysia to establish gēn, where he reinterprets traditional Malaysian ingredients and flavours through contemporary techniques. His work has received recognition from the Michelin Guide, including the Michelin Guide Young Chef Award, and Asia’s 50 Best Restaurants.

The collaboration will feature a specially curated dinner menu exploring Malaysian culinary heritage, regional traditions and food memories.

Ranjit Batra, CEO, Ventive Hospitality Ltd, said, “At JW Marriott Pune, we are committed to creating distinctive culinary experiences that bring together diverse food cultures, celebrated culinary talent and meaningful stories. Collaborations such as this allow us to introduce our guests to new perspectives on gastronomy while celebrating the heritage and creativity that shape each chef’s approach. Chef Johnson Wong’s interpretation of Malaysian cuisine through the lens of personal identity and heritage makes this a special addition to Tao-Fu’s culinary calendar. We look forward to welcoming him and sharing this experience with our guests.”

data.title: IHCL installs 500-kW solar power plant at Taj Fort Aguada in Goa
data.description:
Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) has installed a 500-kW solar power plant at Taj Fort Aguada Resort & Spa, Goa, as part of its Paathya ESG+ framework.

The installation is expected to generate between 6,00,000 and 7,00,000 kWh of clean energy annually, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 492 to 574 tonnes each year. The project is aimed at lowering the property's reliance on conventional power sources, improving energy efficiency and strengthening energy resilience.

Ranjit Phillipose, Senior Vice President – Operations, IHCL, said, “The installation of the solar power plant at Taj Fort Aguada Resort & Spa, Goa, reflects IHCL's ongoing efforts to integrate sustainable practices into hotel operations. As we continue to advance our Paathya guidance, initiatives such as these, help strengthen energy resilience, improve operational efficiency and support our commitment to responsible hospitality.”

The project forms part of IHCL's wider efforts to expand renewable energy use across its portfolio and reduce its environmental footprint.

data.title: Britannia CMO Puneet Das Quits Within 10 Months Of Joining
data.description:
The former Tata Consumer Products executive is leaving the FMCG major to pursue an opportunity outside the organisation

Puneet Das has resigned as Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries, less than 10 months after joining the company. He will be relieved of his responsibilities with effect from the close of business on December 9, 2026.

In a regulatory filing on November 27, Britannia said Das had decided to pursue an opportunity outside the organisation. His resignation follows his appointment as CMO, effective February 16, 2026.

Das brings over 24 years of experience across the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector, spanning India and international markets. Before joining Britannia, he spent more than eight years at Tata Consumer Products, where he held senior leadership positions, including President and Senior Vice-President, Packaged Beverages.

His earlier career includes leadership stints at Marico, PepsiCo India and GSK Consumer Healthcare India. Over the years, he has worked on several prominent brands, including 7Up, Boost, Horlicks, Tata Tea and Tetley.

A graduate of XLRI Jamshedpur, Das has built his career across marketing, commercial strategy, brand development and business growth.

Britannia has not announced a successor to Das.

data.title: Dyti Dawn Joins DBS Bank As Vice President, Learning And Development
data.description:
After senior posts at Alivus Life Sciences, FocusU Engage and Mahindra, Dawn brings over a decade of HR and learning experience to DBS Bank

Dyti Dawn has joined DBS Bank in Mumbai as Vice President of Learning and Development, taking up the role in November 2026. She brings over a decade of HR and L&D experience across industries such as pharmaceuticals, automotive manufacturing and e-learning. Most recently, Dawn led talent management and capability-building programmes at Alivus Life Sciences (formerly Glenmark Life Sciences). Her appointment comes as DBS emphasises workforce upskilling – the bank itself notes that “upskilling and reskilling has been a key focus for the bank”. Dawn’s learning and development background aligns with this agenda, as the bank continues to invest in employee training and development.

Alivus Life Sciences Role

From February 2023 until October 2026, Dawn was Lead – Corporate HR and Capability Building at Alivus Life Sciences. In that role, she oversaw talent development and organisational capability initiatives. She helped build functional, behavioural and leadership training tracks, and managed succession planning and leadership pipelines. She also supported the roll-out of development programmes across the company’s Mumbai operations, designing workshops and mentoring schemes to enhance leadership effectiveness and employee experience.

FocusU Engage Experience

Earlier, Dawn spent almost four years at FocusU Engage, a Bengaluru-based learning and development firm. As part of her role in learning experience design and category management, she launched an online e‑learning platform and guided the creation of self-paced courses in personal and leadership effectiveness. She introduced a microlearning category and developed interactive workshops. Dawn also designed blended learning journeys and simulations for corporate clients in technology, legal and FMCG sectors, helping to address needs in onboarding, high-potential development and strategic thinking.

Mahindra & Mahindra Roles

Dawn’s career began in the automotive sector with Mahindra & Mahindra. She spent nearly six years in the Mahindra Group’s automotive division in various HR and talent roles. At Mahindra Rise (the dealer channel arm), she led capability-building programmes for dealer network partners nationwide, including the launch of a mobile learning academy for frontline sales and service staff.

She later served as an HR business partner in the eastern region, overseeing recruitment, performance management and retention for field operations. Earlier in her tenure (2013–2014), she was part of the group HR team in Mumbai, where she worked on talent management projects including diversity and inclusion initiatives and the development of a finance leadership pipeline.

Education And Qualifications

Dawn holds a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Human Resource Management from the Symbiosis Centre for Management and Human Resource Development (SCMHRD) at Symbiosis International University, Pune. She earned a Bachelor of Technology degree in Information Technology from the National Institute of Technology, Raipur.

data.title: Kothari Industrial, Thiagarajar College to set up drone training and R&D centres in Madurai
data.description:
Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited and the Thiagarajar College of Engineering signed two Memoranda of Understanding on Friday to establish a Remote Pilot Training Organisation and a dedicated Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Research and Development (R&D) Centre in Madurai.

The dual-pillar partnership bridges century-old industrial leadership with premier engineering academia. The initiative is poised to democratise access to certified drone aviation training while catalysing indigenous research in Defence, surveillance, and disaster-response robotics across Tamil Nadu, the release says.

Under the strategic alliance, both institutions will pool their infrastructure, technical expertise, and human capital to build an end-to-end UAV ecosystem anchored in TCE’s Department of Mechatronics, the release said.

data.title: Lifco Buys Italy's EG Medical For Undisclosed Terms
data.description:
STOCKHOLM (dpa-AFX) - Swedish conglomerate Lifco AB (1L3.F, LIFCO_B.ST) announced on Friday that it has agreed to acquire all shares in Italy-based EG Medical S.r.l., a manufacturer of trays for surgical instruments. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Lifco said the acquisition is not expected to have a significant impact on its earnings or financial position in the 2026 financial year.

EG Medical reported 2025 net sales of approximately 11.9 million euros, according to Lifco.

The company, which employs 32 people, will become part of Lifco's Dental business area, with consolidation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Shares of Lifco were up 0.21% at 287.20 kronor in Stockholm trading.

data.title: Promising Prospects Seen for U.S. Soybean Meal Exports — Market Talk
data.description: While U.S. soybean export sales fell last week, soybean cake and meal sales jumped to 543,500 metric tons from 198,100 tons the week before, with Spain, Italy and Poland among the principal buyers. With three of the top four buyers being EU countries, the purchases could show diversification is on importers' minds as EU deforestation regulation is set to kick in at the end of the year, Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. "While a single week's sales data are not sufficient to establish a trend, the U.S. is widely viewed as one of the best-positioned suppliers to capture incremental EU demand due to its relatively favorable traceability and deforestation profile compared to South American competitors." Soybean meal is up 2.3% on CBOT. Soybeans are up 2.1%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: Canada's budget deficit over first six months of 2026/27 shrinks to C$10.50 billion
data.description:
OTTAWA, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Canada's budget deficit in the first six months of the 2026/27 fiscal year shrank to C$10.50 billion ($7.38 billion) as government revenues grew faster than expenses, the finance ministry said on Friday. By comparison, the deficit in the same period a year earlier had been C$16.10 billion, it said in a statement. Year-to-date revenues grew by 6.9%, largely reflecting higher income from personal income taxes and higher GST revenues. Program expenses rose 4.9%, driven by higher transfers for government programs and increased operating costs. Public debt increased by 9.3% largely reflecting higher average effective interest rates on an increased stock of marketable bonds, the ministry said. On a monthly basis, the deficit was slightly up to C$5.14 billion, compared to a C$5.02 billion deficit in September 2025. ($1 = 1.4231 Canadian dollars) (Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, editing by David Ljunggren) ((Reuters Ottawa bureau; david.ljunggren@tr.com))

data.title: Black Friday came early for retailers as Thanksgiving delivered record $7.1B in sales
data.description:
Shoppers chasing double-digit discounts on electronics, toys, sporting goods, and apparel turned Thanksgiving into a record day for retailers—and put Black Friday on pace for one too.

Adobe Analytics found that shoppers worked off their Thanksgiving gluttony online, spending a record $7.1B online—up 10.4% from last year. That still trails the forecasts for Black Friday ($12.9B) and Cyber Monday ($15.1B), but Thanksgiving’s growth rate beat both.

Adobe credits this to deep discounts that were pulled forward from Black Friday and Cyber Monday. The biggest discounts were on electronics and toys, with attractive offers for everything else, including furniture and appliances, and expected to become even more appealing during Black Friday.

No doubt Grand Theft Auto VI drove a surge in gaming sales, with the sale of consoles soaring more than 1,000% (GTA VI is only compatible with certain consoles). Triple-digit percentage gains were also seen in video games and accessories.

And while Cyber Monday is typically the day shoppers’ cash in on deals for electronics, sales on Thanksgiving were equally impressive with buyers scooping up smartphones, headphones, smartwatches, TVs, and other smart appliances, driving sales up by 250% to more than 600% from last year.

The proliferation of AI shopping bots generated more purchases and created larger carts and reportedly drove a 92% increase in revenue per visit compared to non-AI traffic. The use of AI also means fewer returns for retailers to handle after the holidays. Adobe found that one-third of respondents were less likely to return an item that they found using AI.

Shoppers also took advantage of the Buy-Now-Pay-Later (BNPL) option, increasing by 5.1% from last year and expected to drive a record $1.09B in online spending on Cyber Monday.

Extrapolating Thanksgiving spending to the next major shopping days of the holiday season, Adobe expects Black Friday spending to reach another record of $12.9B—or $13.7M per minute between 10am and 2pm—and Cyber Monday to a record $15.1B, adding to the $47.5B expected to be spent during Cyber Week (5-day period including Thanksgiving).

Some of the top sellers are Pokémon Pikachu Puppertronic, squishies, LEGO Pokémon Smart Play, Grand Theft Auto VI , Madden NFL 27 (EA), Nintendo Switch 2 , PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series S/X , iPhone Duo , Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 , Oura Ring (OURA), AirPods , and Ray-Ban Meta smartglasses.

The takeaway: Thanksgiving was just the warm-up. Between pulled-forward deals, GTA VI mania, and AI doing the shopping, retailers are headed for their biggest Cyber Week ever.

data.title: Global markets rally as end of bruising month approaches
data.description:
Key points:
  • US stocks rise to end week
  • Chinese stocks jump more than 4% on new support measures
  • Investors still expect Fed to raise rates in December

By Harry Robertson and Stella Qiu

Global stock markets rallied on Friday, with Chinese shares bouncing back from a one-year low and US indexes rising to open a holiday-shortened session.

Japan's Nikkei jumped 2.1% overnight, while MSCI's index of Asian shares excluding Japan (.MISX00000PUS) climbed 1.8%. European stocks rose 1%, adding to their gains on Thursday, when US markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.

On Friday morning, the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.5% and the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX added 1.1%.

The action amounted to a reprieve for what has turned into a hair-raising November for global equities, particularly in the once-hot technology sector, where monthly declines have ranged from 14% for the Korean Kospi and 9% for the Nikkei to 6% for the Nasdaq Composite and less than 1% for the Stoxx 600. US stocks will close on Friday at 1 p.m. ET (1800 GMT), leaving Monday as the final trading session for what has been a volatile period.

"There doesn’t appear to be any clear catalyst for the sudden turn in the market mood, leaving us somewhat skeptical about the longevity of this latest shift," analysts at Scotiabank said on Friday.

Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP, said that "the risk of a deeper correction at some point in the next six months remains high" despite the executive-suite U-turn that brought Jensen Huang back to chipmaker Nvidia , the resilient US economy, strong corporate profit growth and December being a seasonally stronger period for shares.

MORE STATE SUPPORT IN CHINA

China's blue chips gained 4.2%, a day after hitting their lowest since June 2025, as the cabinet rolled out more support for capital markets, calling for a greater role by state-backed "national team" investors.

Global equities have slid in erratic trading in recent weeks as doubts have crept in about whether huge rallies in AI stocks will be justified by future earnings.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 traded roughly 20% lower than its October record high on Wednesday, before rebounding later in the session. MSCI's all-world stock index is down 5% for the month EURONEXT:IACWI.

Huang's dramatic departure from and return to Nvidia has been a major source of volatility.

Shares in the $3.6 trillion company surged 31% when Huang was reinstated on Monday but remain down 27% for the month.

Nvidia remained a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.

TREASURIES GIVE UP GAINS

US Treasuries have gained as the stock selloff has pushed investors towards safe-haven assets, but were on the back foot on Friday as equities rallied.

The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield rose 5 basis points to 4.90%, putting it roughly flat for the week after a sharp drop a week earlier. Yields move inversely to prices.

The US dollar was flat on the day but headed for a third monthly gain that has pushed it to its highest since March 2025.

Expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December have boosted the currency, as have safe-haven flows.

The euro was little changed after news that Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos would become the next president of the European Central Bank, a well-telegraphed move that suggested policy continuity. European yields ticked higher.

Futures imply a 99% chance the Fed will raise rates in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded and markets are now on guard for what might happen if stocks continue to pull back over the next month. (0#USDIRPR)

"The Fed could, of course, still blink," said David Rees, chief economist at Schroders. But "if growth and inflation data remain firm, in a game of cat and mouse, markets could soon begin pricing a more hawkish Fed back in, potentially setting off the same chain of events all over again."

Oil prices were heading for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude futures rose to a more than two-week high of $98 a barrel on Friday before pulling back to trade around $95. They were down around 19% for the month.

data.title: Elia Group Raises 2026 Net Profit Guidance
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - Elia Group SA/NV (ELI.BR, ELIAF), a Belgian electricity transmission operator, announced on Friday that it had raised its full-year 2026 net profit guidance, supported by higher interest rates that are expected to boost remuneration from its regulated activities in Belgium and Germany.

The company now expects net profit attributable to Elia Group shareholders to range between €730 million and €760 million, compared with its previous forecast of €690 million to €740 million. The revised outlook includes approximately €65 million in negative adjusted items, mainly related to its US investments, after hybrid coupons.

Elia Group shares were up 0.08 percent at €132.50 on the Brussels Stock Exchange.

data.title: Brazilian Real Rallies as Lula Names Market-Friendly Finance Minister — Market Talk
data.description:
1050 ET - The Brazilian real is recovering against the U.S. dollar after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva appointed the chairman of Bradesco Bank as his next finance minister. The slide in the real following Lula's surprise re-election win last month put downward pressure on U.S. soybean prices on concerns that Brazilian exporters would have a large exchange advantage over U.S. producers. Soybeans are up 2.1% on CBOT in a broad rally that has corn advancing 1.5% and wheat up 0.9%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

0959 ET - Corporate bonds look favorable given the sound credit profiles of issuers and cheap bond prices, RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Mark Dowding says in a note. Wide credit spreads offer opportunities to buy the assets at affordable valuations, Dowding says. RBC BlueBay Asset Management also expects debt default rates to stay contained due to the low risk of economic recession. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0847 ET - Canada shoots down a call from the province of Ontario and Unifor, the union representing the country's autoworkers, to exempt motor-vehicle manufacturers from a federal industrial carbon tax. The demand by Ontario and Unifor is an effort to persuade Stellantis to rethink its plan to sell a Toronto-area factory. "Claims that industrial carbon pricing harms domestic auto manufacturing are misleading," says Canadian Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin. She adds federal greenhouse-gas emission standards for vehicles don't apply to Canadian-built vehicles destined for export, which Dabrusin says cover the vast majority of vehicles Stellantis produces in Canada. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

0725 ET - Gross government bond issuance in the eurozone is expected to rise 4% on year to a record high of 1.496 trillion euros in 2027, according to LBBW's Elmar Voelker. "Another record year for government borrowing is likely to be avoided only if the consolidation of public finances receives an unexpected boost from a significant acceleration in economic growth," the senior fixed income analyst says. For the second year in a row, Germany is set to account for about half of the projected increase in gross issuance, he says, forecasting that the country will increase gross supply on the capital market by just under 10% to 380 billion euros. Maturities are set to rise nearly 5% to 945 billion euros next year, also driving supply. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0703 ET - The macroeconomic data flow is expected to remain on the bond-bearish side next week, LBBW's Elmar Voelker says in a note. Eurozone inflation might have stabilized at around 4% in November, with falling energy prices providing some relief, the senior fixed-income analyst says. "Initial data from France and Spain even suggest that hopes for an easing of inflation pressures may be justified," he says, However, the core rate is likely to have risen for the third month in a row, he adds. In the U.S., attention will be primarily focused on November labor-market data, Voelker says. LBBW expects solid growth of around 100,000 jobs and a stable unemployment rate. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0640 ET - Artificial intelligence companies are expected to issue more debt in 2027, after record level supply so far in 2026, RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Mark Dowding says in a note. However, the pace of acceleration in debt issuance could be more modest than previously expected due to increased public backlash against AI buildout, he says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0610 ET - While the most dramatic phase of interest-rate increases is now behind us, the era of ultra-low rates appears to be over, says Yves Bonzon, group chief investment officer at Julius Baer. "The return to a more normal cost of capital is reshaping investment markets and exposing important differences between private and public sector balance sheets," he says in a note. Households and corporations have generally proven more resilient than expected, but governments face mounting pressure from higher refinancing costs and rising debt burdens, he adds. "As a result, fiscal sustainability and debt management are becoming increasingly important considerations for policymakers and investors alike." Julius Baer continues to favor high-quality corporate credit and local-currency emerging market debt, "both of which benefit from comparatively stronger balance sheets." (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0550 ET - The European Central Bank's leadership change is unlikely to alter the near-term policy outlook and has no material implication for the euro, says Brown Brothers Harriman's Elias Haddad in a note. "The ECB Governing Council is not a one-person show; 21 members have voting rights, including six Executive Board members and 15 governors of the national central banks," the global head of markets strategy says. Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president, while Germany's Markus Brunnermeier is expected to replace Philip Lane as chief economist and France's Laurence Boone is set to take over the ECB's market operations role from Isabel Schnabel. The euro is trading flat against the dollar at $1.0964. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0536 ET - The Federal Reserve still has a long way to go to get inflation back to its 2% target, but "fortunately, the Fed's hawkish policy stance is intact and supportive of U.S. dollar," Brown Brothers Harriman's Elias Haddad says in a note. "An equity correction alone is unlikely to stop the Fed from tightening," the global head of markets strategy says. "If the Fed blinks, its credibility takes a hit, and the dollar will slide," he says. BBH expects the turning point for the dollar will come when tighter policy starts to bite into U.S. growth, and markets begin to price in Fed cuts, Haddad says. The DXY dollar index rises 0.2% to 103.855. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0536 ET - Stabilization in artificial-intelligence stocks could enable sterling to strengthen against the dollar, Ebury's Matthew Ryan says in a note. Sterling weakness versus the dollar could fade as market volatility subsides and demand for safe-haven assets like the dollar cools down, Ryan says. The U.K. economy stays resilient and market expectations of additional Bank of England interest-rate rises should support sterling, he says. Sterling rises 0.1% against the dollar to $1.3124. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0457 ET - RBC BlueBay Asset Management continues to expect that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December and then one more time in the first quarter, fixed income chief investment officer Mark Dowding says. Thereafter, the Fed would go on hold, "as long as inflation can be seen starting to decline from its peak," he says. BlueBay reckons that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will be content with inflation if he can lower it to the high 2% levels. "There is a growing body of argument seeming to advocate for a bit more leniency with respect to the Fed's 2% inflation target, at a time when there is an unprecedented pace of business investment spending in a critical new technology," Dowding says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0454 ET - U.S. technology restrictions present a more pressing challenge to China than tariffs, HSBC says in a research note. Tighter restrictions on access to U.S.-controlled chips in Southeast Asia data centers are "inevitably creating near-term challenges for mainland Chinese AI companies seeking additional computing power," the bank says. Data centers outside China also face tighter rules if they want to provide mainland Chinese companies with computing capacity above a specified threshold, it says. That being said, it will also strengthen mainland China's long-term goal of reducing reliance on foreign technology and supporting domestic chip makers, HSBC says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

data.title: Ujjivan SFB gets RBI nod for 3-month extension of Carol Furtado as interim CEO
data.description:
Ujjivan Small Finance Bank Ltd on Friday (November 27) said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved a three-month extension of Carol Furtado's term as Interim Chief Executive Officer (CEO), effective December 1, 2026.

In a regulatory filing, the bank said the extension will remain in effect until February 28, 2027, or until the appointment of a regular Managing Director (MD) and CEO, whichever is earlier. The approval was communicated through an RBI letter dated November 27, 2026, the bank said.

The bank's board has earlier appointed Carol Furtado, currently an Executive Director and Whole-Time Director at Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, as acting MD and CEO with effect from September 1, 2026.

Furtado has more than three decades of banking experience across business, strategy, operations, people and institutional functions. She has been part of Ujjivan's leadership team and has held her current executive director role at the bank.

Second Quarter Results

Ujjivan Small Finance Bank reported a nearly threefold jump in net profit for the September quarter, even as its board approved a ₹409.04 crore preferential share issue, with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) set to receive the largest allocation.

The small finance bank's net profit rose to ₹365 crore in the second quarter, compared with ₹122 crore in the year-ago period. Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 35.4% year on year to ₹1,248.4 crore from ₹921.7 crore.

Asset quality improved marginally on a sequential basis. Gross non-performing assets (NPA) declined to 2.10% from 2.16% in the previous quarter, while net NPA fell to 0.31% from 0.34%.

Provisions stood at ₹103 crore, down from ₹127.3 crore in the June quarter and ₹235 crore in the year-ago period. However, other operating expenses increased to ₹438 crore from ₹347.3 crore a year earlier.

The bank's total deposits grew 29% year on year to ₹50,643 crore, compared with ₹39,211 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 26%.

He added that the bank’s gross loan book grew 32.1% year on year to ₹45,699 crore, while the share of secured assets increased to 52.1%. Deposits rose 29.2% to ₹50,643 crore, crossing the ₹50,000 crore milestone. Funding diversification also continued, with the bank increasing its securitisation pool by ₹500 crore in October.

Shares of Ujjivan Small Finance Bank Ltd ended at ₹57.45, up by ₹0.45, or 0.79%, on the BSE.

data.title: SEBI grants Tata Steel extension till December 8 for detailed public statement on APL Apollo Tubes open offer
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has granted Tata Steel an extension of seven days, till December 8, 2026, to publish the detailed public statement regarding its open offer to acquire up to 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes Limited, according to a stock exchange filing on Friday.

Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited, the manager to the open offer, informed the exchanges that the market regulator had granted the extension following a request submitted by Tata Steel. The company was originally required to publish the detailed public statement in newspapers on or before December 1, 2026, in accordance with SEBI's takeover regulations. SEBI, through an email dated November 27, permitted Tata Steel "to publish the detailed public statement in relation to the Open Offer on or before December 8, 2026, instead of December 1, 2026," the filing said.

However, the deadline for filing the draft letter of offer with the market regulator remains unchanged. "The last date for filing the draft letter of offer with SEBI remains unchanged, i.e., December 8, 2026," the filing added. The development comes on a day when SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey emphasised that the market regulator takes minority shareholders' rights "very seriously" while responding to a question on investor concerns surrounding the proposed Tata Steel-APL Apollo Tubes transaction.

"Our things are very clear because minority shareholders' interest is extremely important for us," Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of an ASSOCHAM conference in New Delhi. Institutional investors and proxy advisory firms have raised concerns that the proposed transaction structure could place a disproportionate share of the financial cost and risk on APL Apollo's minority shareholders.

Earlier this week, Tata Steel announced plans to acquire a maximum 52.38 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes for approximately ₹32,266 crore through a promoter stake purchase and a mandatory open offer. Under the proposed transaction, Tata Steel will acquire a 26.38 per cent stake from APL Apollo's promoter group for approximately ₹15,510.61 crore, while making an open offer to acquire an additional 26 per cent stake from public shareholders for up to ₹16,755.66 crore.

data.title: RBI reverses October CRR tightening, eases daily reserve maintenance norm
data.description:
With the liquidity situation in the banking system swinging from surplus to deficit in the last four months, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to restore the status quo on minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) with effect from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026.

The RBI said the minimum daily maintenance of CRR by Banks will be reduced from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent. This comes in view of liquidity tightness in the banking system.

The central bank had raised the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 90 per cent of the requirement to 99 per cent effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026.

The October step was necessitated as Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions were not proving enough to neutralise the surplus Rupee liquidity generated due to the US Dollar-Rupee Forex Swap facility that RBI provided for fresh FCNR (B) deposits mobilised by banks (from June 8 to August 31, 2026).

With the latest announcement, RBI has restored the status quo on the minimum daily maintenance of CRR in two months. CRR is the slice of deposits that banks have to park with the RBI. This ratio is currently at 3 per cent. Resources deployed as CRR do not earn interest.

Liquidity Relief

V Rama Chandra Reddy, Head - Treasury, Karur Vysya Bank, said, “The RBI’s decision to restore the minimum daily CRR requirement to 90 per cent from 99 per cent, effective December 1, is a welcome relief for banks. It eases the tightrope in day-to-day CRR management, provides greater operational flexibility and helps moderate liquidity pressures.”

“Interestingly, despite the tighter compliance requirement, banks have continued to maintain substantial SDF (Standing Deposit Facility) balances, reflecting the uneven distribution of liquidity and limited flexibility under the 99 per cent regime,” he added.

He emphasised that while this move will not inject additional liquidity into the banking system, it will provide banks greater flexibility in managing CRR requirements and optimising funds, potentially resulting in lower SDF balances as they manage CRR requirements efficiently.

K Arvind, Head - Treasury, Tamilnad Mercantile Bank, said, “This move provides some operational flexibility in maintaining daily CRR. Banks were keeping excess CRR to ensure that there is no slip-up in complying with the statutory ratio.”

data.title: China’s big tech value falls to record-low share of U.S. peers
data.description:
China’s biggest technology companies have continued to lose ground to their U.S. counterparts during the market selloff, with their combined market value falling to a record-low 11.6% of that of Alphabet , Amazon , and Meta Platforms , according to market strategist Rob Anderson.

The combined market capitalization of Baidu , Alibaba , and Tencent stood at $829.78B as of Nov. 25, compared with $7.14T for the three U.S. technology companies, data from Ned Davis Research showed.

That put the Chinese group’s value at 11.63% of its U.S. peers, the lowest since at least September 2014, when the Ned Davis Research data begin.

The latest reading is well below the 40.61% average for the ratio over the full period, according to the chart. The ratio came close to 80% in 2015 and again in 2020-21 before its subsequent decline.

data.title: These stocks soared the most during a wild week highlighted by Huang's return to Nvidia
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Nvidia's stock soared this week, but was still down nearly 28% for November and 21% for 2026

The return of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as the company's CEO on Nov. 23 helped drive the entire U.S. stock market higher this week.

The broad U.S. stock indexes were all green early on Friday, as investors were closer to capping off a week of remarkable gains, sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO. Still, the gains only partially offset the previous week's declines.

The S&P 500 SPX was up 0.7% in early trading Friday, for a gain of 4.6% for the week as almost all of its components contributed. But that follows a decline of 8.6% the previous week through Friday, Nov. 20.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA was also up 0.7% early Friday, for a one-week gain of 4.9%, following a decline of 8% the previous week.

The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP) rose 0.8% early Friday and was up 5.1% for the week, following a 10% decline the previous week.
